[LSER.9.3.1] Series state eviction policy is backing-specific.
All-time backings (running-stats, all-time distinct-set, etc.)
live until engine shutdown — eviction would destroy cumulative
semantics. Sliding and tumbling backings evict when no
sample for that identity has been absorbed for the declared
window — after window-of-silence the backing holds zero
in-window samples and the per-key allocation is pure overhead.

The state a signal aggregation ([LSIG.1.1]) reads is the exception: the engine
**must not** evict it after a window of silence. `active_fraction`, `onset_rate`
and `integral` read the slot as a step function, each absorbed value held until
the next ([LSIG.1.3.1], [LSIG.3.2]), so a silent window is not an empty one.
The last absorbed value, any open interval and `t_first` ([LSER.19.7]) persist
for the instance's life.
